summary: Raw material for the accretionary class is open (MorphoSource keyword hits: 1,195 shell, 82 claw, 45 horn, 25 tusk; 1,840 iNaturalist Nautilus photos) and for the simultaneous class as herbarium images (iDigBio, about 39.9 million imaged plant records), but no source provides outlines or spiral-fit annotations and no dataset pairs the two classes with an accretion label. Spiral-deviation methodology papers exist on Zenodo, with no outline tables confirmed.
next_step: Choose a fixed sample (e.g. gastropod and Nautilus shells, tusks and horns from MorphoSource vs. leaves from a labelled herbarium subset and fish outlines), pre-register the spiral-fit criterion and the accretion/simultaneous labelling rule, then extract outlines.
obstacles_confirmed: Keyword counts in MorphoSource mix many element types; the spiral-bearing subset is smaller and was not counted.
Labelling a structure as 'simultaneously formed' needs developmental knowledge that no dataset records.
